svg.text: The device key inside the CONNECT packet: readable in the clear
Concept 10 · MQTT on port 1883 isn't encrypted yet · Node 1's first packet carries the username and its key as they are
Node 1's CONNECT packet (MQTT 3.1.1), byte by byte
packet type CONNECT, then 117 byte more
flags: there is a username, a password, and a will
gray = the two byte length bytes: 00 0c = 12, 00 17 = 23, 00 2b = 43 (warm-up step 5)
white = the contents: each character one byte, for example 61 = a and 34 = 4
red = the device key: readable in full, with no key at all to unlock it (this module's example key)
still acceptable for the time being, because:
your home Wi-Fi is already encrypted between the device
the broker can't be knocked on from the internet: there is no
port forwarding to the Pi or your laptop
so a sniffer must already be inside
your network: the risk is real, but small
required before the broker is opened to the internet:
the whole connection is encrypted, including
the CONNECT packet: the key can't be read anymore
on the internet, messages pass through many networks owned by
other people, and an open broker is knocked on by
an even stronger way, a certificate for
every device (mTLS), is discussed in the Technical Deep Dive
